plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one short, high-value full-body session each week. Week 1 establishes a baseline on the main lower-body lift so future loading can be set more accurately, and the main training starts in Week 2. With only one S&C session per week and a 30-minute cap, the plan keeps power first, then main strength, then simple accessories that support punching posture, trunk stiffness, and general athletic development without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general lower-body force, simple explosive ability, and trunk strength with low-complexity work that fits around boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main strength work and keep power sharp with small weekly load increases and controlled fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift toward faster intent and sharper power expression while holding onto the strength built earlier.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quiet landing. Reset between reps and stop if height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low box and land softly in a stable stance.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with a few easy ramping sets, then do one hard set of 5 clean reps with the heaviest load you can control with solid depth and posture. This sets your starting baseline for the next weeks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can track your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Record the best clean top set and keep technique strict.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the goblet hold limits load before the legs do.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a version you can do with clean body line and full control. Stop with 1-2 good reps left.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Raise the hands on a bench or box if full floor reps are not clean yet.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if wrists or shoulders dislike push-ups.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Pull the elbow toward the hip and pause briefly at the top. Keep the torso still.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if lower-back support is needed.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squeeze glutes, and keep ribs down. End the set before the low back sags.

substitutionOptions.name: Hard-Style Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the plank position is uncomfortable on the shoulders.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump fast and land softly. Take enough rest to keep each rep crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low box and step down each rep.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use the Week 1 result to choose a challenging but controlled load. Keep the tempo smooth and leave 2 reps in reserve.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your heaviest clean set of 6 with full depth and stable posture.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the goblet hold becomes the limiting factor.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Move explosively up and control the way down. Stop before body position breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if full push-ups are still inconsistent.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you need a simpler loaded press.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Drive the elbow back without twisting the torso. Lower under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want more upper-back focus with less setup.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.notes: Stand tall and do not lean toward the weight. Walk slowly and keep the trunk braced.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Arm Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if space is limited. Hold for 20-30 seconds each side.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Every rep should look the same. Stop if the jumps feel heavy or slow.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Keep the box height conservative and land balanced.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the heaviest clean set of 5 you can complete without losing depth or posture.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if available load or comfort is better with two dumbbells.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Keep the body rigid and press hard through the floor. Use a harder variation only if all reps stay clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a more stable pressing option.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Reach long at the bottom, then row smoothly without shrugging.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you prefer a simpler setup.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.notes: Stay tall, keep the ribs stacked, and do not rush the walk.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Arm Hold

exercises.name: Goblet Squat

performanceTarget.prompt: Log your cleanest work set and note whether it felt easier than last week.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat

exercises.name: Push-Up

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you need an easier option this deload week.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if push-ups irritate the wrists.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Smooth pull, brief pause, controlled lower. Do not chase fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use for an easier, low-fatigue setup.

exercises.name: Front Plank

substitutionOptions.name: Hard-Style Dead Bug
